oewn-00007846-n.learner: a human being; one man, woman, or child
examples: a person who can write a long letter with ease cannot write ill
a person unconnected with any of us, and, comparatively speaking, a stranger to our family

oewn-05224944-n.learner: someone's body, usually counting the clothes they have on
examples: I have heard much of your master's fine person
A weapon was hidden on his person.

oewn-06337790-n.learner: a grammar class that sorts pronouns, possessive words, and verb forms by whether they point to the speaker, the one spoken to, or someone else
examples: In grammar, "I" is the first person and "you" is the second person.
Stop talking about yourself in the third person.

oewn-00725507-v.learner: to make room in your plans for something that might happen, or to admit that something is true or sound
examples: Mrs. Hurst and her sister allowed it to be so
allowing for the loss of Sir William, and there being only one card-table in the evening

oewn-00803980-v.learner: to agree to something, or to give someone permission to do it
examples: Will you allow me, or do I ask too much, to introduce my sister to your acquaintance during your stay at Lambton?
Allow me, by the way, to observe, my fair cousin, that I do not reckon the notice and kindness of Lady Catherine de Bourgh as among the least of the advantages in my power to offer.

oewn-02427979-v.learner: to do something, or to leave something undone, so that another thing can happen
examples: I would not on any account trifle with her affectionate solicitude, or allow her to hear it from anyone but myself.
This sealed door won't allow the water to come into the basement.

oewn-00128838-s.learner: coming straight after this one in time or in order
examples: When is your next ball to be, Lizzy?
Scarcely anything was talked of the whole day or next morning but their visit to Rosings.

oewn-00449506-s.learner: closest in space or position, right beside it with nothing in between
examples: She could hear their voices in the next room.
The man in the next seat handed her the book.

oewn-00129027-s.learner: said of a day of the week, meaning the coming one, or the one after that
examples: Not this Saturday, next Saturday.
We are to dine with them on Tuesday next.

oewn-01911251-v.learner: to change the way you are facing or the way you are going
examples: Recovering himself, however, shortly, he turned to his partner, and said
she turned suddenly towards him and said

oewn-02632685-v.learner: to go through a change, or to grow into something new
examples: In a single night he turned traitor and went over to the enemy.

oewn-00125649-v.learner: to come little by little into a new state, or to take on a new quality
examples: The days turned colder as autumn went on.
The bread had turned hard by morning.

oewn-15252642-n.learner: a stretch of time equal to one twenty-fourth of a day
examples: He did look at it, and into it, for half an hour
she went upstairs half an hour ago

oewn-15253174-n.learner: the time that the clock shows
examples: at a proper hour they joined the party in Lady Catherine's drawing-room
The hour is getting late.

oewn-15253706-n.learner: a stretch of time that is special and worth remembering
examples: She stood by him in his darkest hour.
It was their finest hour.

oewn-00510460-r.learner: with each other, in each other's company
examples: I hope you will be convinced of it, by seeing them happy together.
We went to the movies together.

oewn-00117698-r.learner: touching each other, or very close to each other
examples: She pressed her hands together and said nothing.
The wet leaves stuck together.

oewn-00117901-r.learner: brought into one place as a group
examples: The whole family was gathered together in the drawing-room.

oewn-05842164-n.learner: what is in your mind; the main thing you are thinking about
examples: Unwilling as she was to admit an idea so destructive to Jane's happiness
The idea of the olive branch perhaps is not wholly new

oewn-05991800-n.learner: what you mean to do; the thing you are aiming at
examples: I think I have understood that Mr. Bingley has not much idea of ever returning to Netherfield again?

oewn-05846174-n.learner: a view that is your own
examples: This was praise of all others most extraordinary, most opposite to her ideas.

oewn-07148409-n.learner: the use of speech to swap views, ideas, or news with someone in an easy, everyday way
examples: Their powers of conversation were considerable.
There could be no conversation in the noise of Mrs. Philips's supper party

oewn-13953278-n.learner: a tie between people that is not as close as friendship
examples: A fortnight's acquaintance is certainly very little.
as far as their acquaintance reached, there was no fault to find

She invited a few acquaintances to dine with her.

oewn-05825271-n.learner: the knowledge you have of someone or something from your own experience of them
examples: Her acquaintance with the Italian language was slight.

oewn-07501369-n.learner: a particular feeling of wanting something
examples: I have no wish of denying that I did everything in my power to separate my friend from your sister

oewn-07200530-n.learner: words that show what you want or would like

oewn-05799610-n.learner: the particular thing you would rather have
examples: It was his last wish that the estate stay in the family.
